Hi Claire — thanks for the clear brief and for sharing the SOW. High level response below; Marissa (solutions) and Ben (CS/account) are looped to fill in technical and commercial detail.

1) EU data residency options
- Hosted w/ EU residency (tenant pinning): low friction, fastest time-to-value; adds a residency surcharge (I outline options in the attached spreadsheet).
- Private (VPC/on-prem) or Dedicated with customer KMS: required if you need strict network controls or on-prem keys. Lead time ~6–10 weeks for Dedicated capacity in eu-west, less for tenant pinning if capacity is available.

2) APAC onramp and burst
- Recommended: staged pilot in APAC (phase 1: routing only, phase 2: warm KV cache + Dedicated burst window). We can support burst with Dedicated pools plus on-demand burst credits; I attached a matrix with commit vs burst economics.

3) Cross-region failover
- Default behavior: encrypted transit; when failing over to eu-west we can rehydrate KV caches from snapshot artifacts and honor SSO/consent flows. For strict residency we can configure a policy that restricts certain data sinks to EU-only even during failover — Marissa will detail the controls.

Hi Claire — adding technical detail on the residency and failover controls so your engineers can validate.

EU residency specifics:
- Isolation: we can pin your tenant to an EU-only cluster (eu-west-1) with customer-managed KMS for envelope encryption. Logs / audit trails are retained in the region and access is restricted by RBAC and IP allowlists.
- Data flows: inference request metadata can be routed for telemetry to US if needed, but payloads and embeddings can be configured to never leave EU.

APAC onramp plan (recommended phases):
1) Pilot (2–4 weeks): spin a small eu-west + ap-southeast staging path. No routing change for live traffic; run test workloads and validations.
2) Warm-up (1 week): provision Dedicated burst pool in ap-southeast, pre-warm model KV cache, run capacity tests (target 3k steady -> 12k burst).
3) Traffic shift (scheduled window): shift 5–10% of sessions, monitor latency/quality, and iterate.

Failover behavior:
- We support weighted routing with policy-based fallback. On failover, session state is reconstructed from last-known KV snapshots; we can optionally replicate non-PII metadata cross-region and keep PII locked to EU-only storage tiers.
- We recommend a DR runbook that includes cache-warm commands and TTLs for ephemeral state to minimize cold starts.

Compliance artifacts we can provide: SOC 2 extracts, KMS key rotation logs, and sample audit events for a simulated failover.

I attached a short APAC onboarding checklist for ops. Happy to review that during the call.

—Marissa
